architecture_checks: 8/8 architecture gates PASS over 156 real cross-context edges (up from 143 at Phase 16 acceptance); all 9 numeric budgets satisfied under ratified measurement contract 1.0.0. execution.workflow and surfaces.command both reached max_public_surface_per_context's 40-of-40 ceiling during this phase (Packages 5 and 6 respectively); acceptance.engine was already at the identical ceiling from an earlier phase. Two real budget/depth hazards were measured and answered by decomposition, never by exception: (1) construct_dispatch.py's ten control constructs were collapsed behind one public evaluate_construct entry point rather than ten separately-public evaluate_* functions, to fit execution.workflow's public-surface budget; (2) a static surfaces.command -> execution.workflow import would have extended the real four-hop execution.workflow -> execution.durable -> control.policy -> kernel.contracts chain to five, breaching max_orchestration_depth - answered with structural Protocols (GraphStoreLike, ExecutorLike) and composition-root-injected factories, the identical shape Phase 16 used for its own depth violation. Package 8's ARK-REQ-0331 coverage check, needing acceptance.engine's now-saturated budget, was placed as a structural cross-check (backend/tests/structural/, the test_contract_drift.py idiom) instead of a new production module - no budget was exceeded, none was excepted. No new declared sibling edge was required this phase; the pre-declared execution.workflow -> execution.durable edge ("workflow steps are durable jobs") was consumed exactly as declared.
duplicate_shadow_check: shadow_registry and duplicate_canonical_authority gates PASS. backend/tests/structural/test_workflow_authority.py (14 tests) proves execution.workflow constructs no second graph model, no second revision store, no second execution-plan cache and declares no state literal outside workflow_execution_state_machine.py's own named constants. workflow_error_mapping.py and workflow.py (surfaces.command) match execution.workflow's errors by exact class name rather than importing the classes, specifically so no shadow-authority import is introduced while still refusing precisely. frontend/src/features/workflow/vocabulary.ts is documented, in its own module docstring, as a UI picklist rather than a shadow of GraphVocabulary: WorkflowGraphDocument.build is the only place either list is ever enforced, and a stale palette entry can only cause the backend to refuse a graph, never to silently accept an invalid one.
security_findings: PROTECTED_CORE profile (ARK-REQ-0111): this phase creates backend/arkali/control/policy/workflow_approval.py and modifies backend/arkali/control/policy/policy_errors.py, and control.policy is a declared Protected Core context - the stronger profile is owed and is not downgradable by declaration (verification_profile.py derives it from the changed-path set alone). All three required categories (security review, adversarial review, full regression) are satisfied by real, zero-exit test executions named above. WorkflowApprovalGate is additive only: no PDP change, no new operation class, no change to any pre-existing control.policy decision - assert_may_record refuses any actor in the already-canonical stable_mutation.prohibited_actors set (workflow was already named there for MS Constitution 6) and is_enforced_approval refuses a non-APPROVED or stale-revision decision. The full backend/tests/security suite (245 passed, up from 233) is green, including the new WorkflowApprovalGate suite (12 tests) proving both refusals in isolation, backend/tests/surfaces/test_command_workflow_api.py's real HTTP 403 for the workflow actor, and frontend/tests/e2e/workflow-studio.spec.ts's fourth, real-browser proof of the identical refusal (ARK-ERR-0133), with the execution provably still WAITING_APPROVAL afterward. No AI provider is contacted anywhere in this phase.
fake_success_scan: No fake-implementation marker; scripts/check_repository_structure.py check 10 PASS. Every node kind dispatches as one real execution.durable job (submit -> begin_attempt -> complete_attempt against real persistence); every control construct's decision is computed from real declared facts (node.parameters, the document's own edges, a persisted counter), never fabricated to make a test pass - construct_dispatch.py's own module docstring states this explicitly. HUMAN APPROVAL cannot be bypassed by a UI affordance: only WorkflowExecutor.approve, gated by WorkflowApprovalGate, may advance WAITING_APPROVAL, proven both by a real HTTP 403 (Package 6) and a real browser-driven refusal (Package 7). No graph-drawing library was added to make the frontend appear more complete than the minimum needed to prove the slice end to end - the canvas is a small, real, pointer-driven implementation, not a vendored dependency standing in for one.
limitations: The Studio's node-kind and control-construct palette (frontend/src/features/workflow/vocabulary.ts) is a hand-maintained picklist, not fetched from a live backend vocabulary endpoint - considered and rejected because both execution.workflow and surfaces.command are at their public-surface ceiling and a stale picklist cannot misinform legality the way the Project lifecycle picklist's dynamic fetch was built to prevent (LifecycleMachineResponse's own rationale); a future VDC change to the canonical list would require a matching frontend edit, caught immediately by test_workflow_ui_coverage.py's exact-count assertion rather than silently drifting. The Studio provides no workflow deletion, no revision diff view and no multi-user collaboration - MS §Visual Workflow Studio requires none of these, and the Build Protocol's "minimum needed to prove the slice end to end" governs scope here exactly as it has for every prior vertical slice. No AI-authored node body exists for the AI/agent/integration kinds; each dispatches as a real durable job whose actual work belongs to whichever future-phase runtime consumes that job type (execution.workflow is not a listed consumer of provider authority) - consistent with Phase 16's own precedent of composing execution without contacting a provider.
blockers: None. No canonical ambiguity required a human ruling. No architecture-budget exception was required; every real budget/depth hazard encountered (construct_dispatch.py's public-surface count, the surfaces.command orchestration-depth extension, and Package 8's acceptance.engine-owned-but-saturated coverage check) was resolved by decomposition under ADR-0008, not by exception.
